title: Review Suikoden Anime First Week
excerpt: A few days ago, several people asked me about my thoughts on the recently released Suikoden II anime, and honestly, I do have a lot of thoughts. More importantly, they're overwhelmingly positive...
content:
A few days ago, several people asked me about my thoughts on the recently released Suikoden II anime, and honestly, I do have a lot of thoughts. More importantly, they're overwhelmingly positive.

To be frank, I never expected the anime to be a one-to-one adaptation of the game. We all knew that simply wasn't going to happen. A direct recreation of a 30+ hour RPG in anime form is unrealistic. Because of that, I went into it expecting changes, and surprisingly, many of those changes are things I actually appreciate.

幻想水滸伝 Suikoden: The Anime • First Week Impressions & Adaptation Breakdown

The Storytelling Works

The first thing I immediately loved was the way they handled the storytelling.

Instead of showing the events at Tenzan Pass chronologically right at the beginning, the anime presents them through flashbacks. We move between Riou and Jowy's present situation after Tenzan Pass and their memories of what happened that night.

I thought that approach was fantastic.

Rather than simply watching the massacre unfold and moving on, we're experiencing it the way the characters do. They're remembering it piece by piece. They wake up, they're trying to process what happened, and the audience uncovers the truth alongside them.

That back-and-forth structure gave the first episode much more emotional weight than a straightforward retelling would have.

The Pacing Doesn't Bother Me

I've seen one of the biggest complaints being that the anime moves too fast.

Personally, I disagree.

The reason Suikoden II felt slower when many of us played it as kids is because we were spending dozens of hours with the game. We explored every town, talked to NPCs, managed inventories, recruited Stars of Destiny, and generally took our time.

An anime doesn't have that luxury.

The creators only have a limited number of episodes and a limited runtime to tell a very large story. They don't have two extra hours to revisit every location or recreate every gameplay moment. That's simply not realistic.

Given the constraints, I actually think the pacing is appropriate. From a narrative perspective, they're moving through material at a speed that makes sense for television.

So when people criticize the anime solely for moving quickly, I don't personally find that to be a convincing criticism. It's adapting a massive RPG. Some level of compression is expected.

Changes I Actually Liked

There are already several notable changes from the game, and most of them worked for me.

The Tenzan Pass Massacre

One of the biggest changes that I haven't seen many people talk about is the implication that the massacre wasn't carried out exclusively by Highland soldiers.

The anime suggests that the Highland forces used Kage assassins to help execute the operation.

Honestly, that makes a lot of sense.

It's nighttime. Armored soldiers are noisy. If you're trying to quietly eliminate an entire unit and frame another nation for it, bringing in professional assassins sounds logical.

It's a small change, but one that actually strengthens the scenario.

Jowy's Background

Another change I really liked involves Jowy.

The anime heavily implies that he already knew he was an adopted son and not a true Atreides by blood. That adds an entirely new layer to his relationship with his father and helps explain some of the resentment directed toward him.

I've always wondered whether Jowy understood why he was treated differently.

A father doesn't normally show that level of disdain toward a child without deeper reasons, especially given everything Jowy and Riou went through.

Making both Riou and Jowy adopted also creates an interesting parallel considering the legacies of the Bright Shield Rune and the Black Sword Rune.

It's a subtle addition, but I think it's a welcome one.

The New Characters Are Interesting

The anime also introduces several characters who were either not present in the original game or are receiving much more attention than expected.

The ones that stood out most to me are:

  • The blue-haired shinobi.
  • His brown-haired companion.
  • Lise, who appears connected to Rowd.
  • The female servant of Luca Blight.
The blue-haired shinobi
His brown-haired companion
Lise (connected to Rowd)
The female servant of Luca Blight

These characters are receiving enough screen time that I don't think it's accidental.

My theory?

I think the anime is going to place greater emphasis on the Stars of Destiny and, more specifically, on Jowy potentially failing to gather all 108 Stars. Yes I think they will feature what was his supposed to be 108 Stars

That's just a theory, and I know some people won't like it, but the focus being given to these new faces makes me think there's a larger narrative purpose behind their introduction.

The Parkour Complaints Are Weird

Another criticism I've seen is about the parkour sequence early in the episode.

Honestly, I think people need to relax.

We're talking about a world with demi-humans, magical runes, giant monsters, and superhuman warriors.

If highly trained soldiers raised under Genkaku's influence can jump across rooftops or move athletically through an environment, that's unacceptable?

Come on.

Besides, there are plenty of other visual changes people barely mention.

For example:

  • Riou and Jowy are wearing pants instead of leggings.
  • The Mercenary Fortress is much larger and on a Hill.
  • Genkaku, Gen, Tomo, and Tuta are introduced earlier.
  • Tuta's role is established almost immediately.

The anime has made many adaptations, both narrative and visual. Most of them feel natural to me.

I'm Just Happy This Exists

More than anything, I'm simply grateful this anime exists.

We live in a timeline where a Suikoden II anime is actually airing.

As a Final Fantasy fan, it's funny to compare this to the FFIX animation project that was announced years ago. It seemed like it had a much larger budget and much bigger ambitions, yet we still haven't seen much come from it.

Meanwhile, Suikoden quietly moved forward and delivered an actual product.

And honestly?

I'm glad I'm still around to watch it.

Looking Ahead

At first, I assumed the anime wouldn't attempt to cover the entire game.

Now, after seeing the first episode, I'm starting to think they actually might.

The question is whether they'll do it in one season, two seasons, or even three.

My rough prediction would be:

  • Season 1: Up to the acquisition of Dunan Castle.
  • Season 2: Building and defending the new alliance, recruiting allies, and navigating the political struggles.
  • Season 3: The escalation of the war, the major tragedies, and the conclusion of Riou and Jowy's story.

Whether that's accurate or not, I have no idea. I haven't looked at any production announcements or press releases.

But from a storytelling perspective, two to three seasons feels like the ideal format.

Final Thoughts

Overall, I really enjoyed the first episode.

I liked the storytelling structure. I liked the pacing. I liked most of the new additions. I liked the character changes. And I appreciate that the creative team seems willing to reinterpret parts of the game instead of treating the anime as a scene-by-scene recreation.

Most importantly, it still feels like Suikoden II.

That's really all I wanted.

So yeah, I'm ready for Episode 2. Let's see where this journey goes.

title: 10/1/26 — Project Kyaro Log Entry
excerpt: Alright, okay. Let me get this off my chest. I'm mostly writing this down as a way to log something that happened in the past regarding Project Kyaro. Looking back at how the early Special K versions were built and how criticism became fuel...
content:
Alright, okay. Let me get this off my chest.

I'm mostly writing this down as a way to log something that happened in the past regarding Project Kyaro. I think it's been over a year now since I watched a video from a fairly popular content creator criticizing the project.

To be clear, it doesn't really bother me anymore. Looking back, I actually understand a lot of the criticism. What many people didn't understand at the time, though, was how the project was being made and the limitations I was working with.

Back then, Project Kyaro wasn't a BepInEx plugin yet. I was using Special K, which was far from the ideal setup for retexturing the game. Unlike today, I didn't have direct access to all the sprite assets. I had to capture them as they appeared during gameplay.

That meant rushing through both games, trying to encounter and capture as many sprites as possible. If I missed a sprite in a specific scene, there was a good chance I wouldn't see it again for quite some time. Special K worked through a texture hashing system, so I couldn't simply extract assets from the game files, upscale them, and put them back. I needed the texture hashes and the captured textures themselves before I could even begin processing them.

So when people looked at those early versions and said the mod didn't look great, honestly, that was a fair criticism. The early versions weren't polished. But at the same time, I was still in Phase 1. The game had only been out for a matter of weeks, and I think some people expected a single person to somehow finish and polish everything immediately.

That was never going to be realistic.

My goal at the time wasn't perfection. My goal was coverage. I needed to get as many sprites processed as possible so I could eventually come back and refine them. I wasn't dealing with one game. I was dealing with Suikoden I and Suikoden II, both of which required a huge amount of work.

I'd be lying if I said that video didn't feel like a gut punch. It did.

But looking at Project Kyaro today and comparing it to where it started, I realize that experience became fuel. One of my biggest personality flaws, or strengths depending on how you look at it, is that criticism, disdain, and sometimes even outright hate can motivate me to push harder. Part of me looked at that criticism and thought, "You know what? Watch me."

In a strange way, it helped push the project further than it might have gone otherwise.

That said, I don't think it's healthy to live entirely on spite. Looking back now, I can acknowledge that the criticism hurt while also recognizing that it ultimately helped me grow both the project and my skills.

And honestly, I'm proud of where Project Kyaro stands today compared to where it began.

I guess the lesson is that sometimes you can take something painful, something discouraging, and turn it into something positive. It doesn't erase the sting, but it gives that experience a purpose.

Anyway, this is really just a log entry.

Yeah, it hurt.

But here we are.

We're good.

content:
I had planned to share this a few months back, but it slipped my mind. Since it’s going to be part of one of my upcoming modification projects anyway, I figured I might as well share it now with the Suikoden community!

Left: Vanilla release map (4:3 aspect with wood border) • Right: Unused widescreen asset discovered in the game archives, mocked up in Viki's teleport menu.

🗺️ Uncovering the Hidden Widescreen Dunan Map

For the commercial release of Suikoden I & II HD Remaster: Gate Rune and Dunan Unification Wars, players received the familiar parchment world map of Dunan that we all know from the classic PSX title, prominently featured when consulting Templeton or requesting teleportation from Viki.

However, buried deep inside the game data files is an intriguing, completely unused set of visual assets. When extracted and reassembled, these disparate components form a much larger, panoramic widescreen (16:9) edition of the Dunan map.

The complete, uncropped widescreen world map reconstructed from raw game file assets, featuring extended coastal topography, mountains, and Sindar runic inscriptions.

☁️ The Cloud "Fog-of-War" System Hypothesis

Alongside the panoramic map texture, the archive contains dedicated cloud overlay layers specifically rendered to obscure distinct geographic territories of the continent.

Development Hypothesis: The developers may have prototyped or planned an active "Fog of War" dynamic map feature, where unexplored kingdoms and hostile regions would remain shrouded beneath decorative parchment clouds until the hero party physically visited or liberated those territories.

While Konami ultimately shipped the remaster with the static, classic map format, the existence of these sliced cloud sprites indicates that interactive map unveiling was either tested or shelved during remaster development.

📜 Cartography & Lore: Deciphering the Sindar Script

One of the most fascinating details in this expanded artwork is located along the western border, just past the mountainous Tinto territory. Several enigmatic glyphs are inked directly into the parchment. While they might initially look like Japanese kana or Norse runes at first glance, community linguists quickly deciphered them:

• Sindar Cipher: G-U-L-A-S-U-L-A-N-D-U

In Suikoden lore, the ancient Sindar Alphabet uses distinct symbols that directly substitute for the Latin alphabet. Phonetically transcribed into Japanese katakana romaji, it reads "Gulasulandu" — literally Grassland (グラスランド), referencing the great Grassland plains west of Dunan where the events of Suikoden III take place!

⚡ Modding Applications & What's Next

At the very least, this restored and assembled map makes for a gorgeous, authentic widescreen alternative background for Viki’s teleportation menu, custom launchers, or high-definition wallpaper packages.

And this is only scratching the surface — there is plenty more tucked away in the HD Remaster game files that I will be sharing and packaging into raw mod assets in future releases. Stay tuned!

The main goal is be able to play the game with less pixels to achieve that HDish/RemasteredISH look so if like your pixels you might to skip on this one.



Requirements:
VULKAN Renderer Support.
Device that has pretty decent hardware and gpu
Retroarch and Beetle PSX HW
Optional : ReSHade

Features:


Upscaled Character portraits
Upscaled BG of certain views in the game
Typeface/Font replacement
Rune/s Texture replacement
xbr filtering on All sprites

Version: Alpha

Instructions:
Install RetroArch and Beetle PSX HW


https://youtu.be/GVOnX9l8OoM

Recommended Folder Structure .

Wherever you decide to place your main BIN / Iso file , it is recommended that it is contained on its own folder because you need two folders to be present in the same directory.


Make sure that the filename of your game MATCHES the Filename that is in the Cue file.

dump the contents texture mod on the texture-replacements folder

Load the game and press f1
Select Options
Make sure the Renderer is VULKAN
software frame buffer: OFF
Internal GPU Resolution : 2x
Texture Filtering : xBR ( preffered is xBR, SABR is also good. Nearest if you want to keep the Pixels)
Track textures: ON
Replace Textures: ON

content:
DeSmuMe has gone to a lot of updates since 0.9.6 and even though the DeSmuMe forum moderators are very much vocal and public about their reservations for Pokémon players, DeSmuMe is still very much lovable for its incomparable compatibility for ds games, as to what and why the hell on earth DeSmuMe forum moderators are very much irritated every time they see the word Pokémon is another story and probably a separate blog entry from this one. This time I will write this down on free verse instead of my usual tabular view like in 0.9.6

The Question?

How do you speed Up DeSmuMe 0.9.7 stable release and svns ? hmmm if you might ask in my opinion the question is actually Wrong , why so? Well if you are not that familiar on how computers work or your premise for computers (PC/MAC/and whatever) are all the same , you better start to think because if at this point if you have such opinion or mindset, you should have not even started to consider using or playing around emulators. The better question is how do you optimize the rendered game speed of DeSmuMe?, and in this case for Pokémon black and white

The BreakPoint ?
Better check your computer for the “implied” minimum requirements to run DeSmuMe, DeSmuMe is pretty much RAM and processor dependent , to check your computer’s capacity and im assuming that you are using windows just go to you control panel and click systems or alternatively for windows vista and 7 just find the shortcut to your “my computer/Computer” and click properties, the minimum requirements based on consortium of the many DeSmuMe players from all the forums and sites seen are 2 Gigabyte memory and at least a dual core processor which means that if you have a 4 Gigabyte Ram and processors like I5 then your Good to go, or if your not logical numbers and sequence , if by knowledge you know that your computer is running of low end processors or has smaller units of ram than those mentioned above, You should start considering No$GBA and mind you that doesn’t mean that DeSmuMe sucks but rather your computer.

Now with all those to consider, let me break down the tips to maximize your gaming experience with DeSmuMe (for Pokémon Black and White )

Tip 1: power settings :
The very first thing you need to make sure of is your power settings most especially to those who use their laptop like me, is to set it on high performance, High Performance setting ensures maximum ram consumption for DeSmuMe to better render game speed. Make sure to plug-in your laptop to a power source and if your are playing longer number of hours on your laptop just remove your battery and run your laptop plugged.

Tip 2: Leave your DeSmuMe Alone
Since DeSmuMe is ram dependent, make sure that you are running DeSmuMe alone, running other programs will make your game’s speed really slow. If you are using guides, it will be much better to read them on notepad instead of MS words. Some browsers like firefox and safari consumes a lot of RAM , so therefore it is not advisable to play any game in DeSmuMe while browsing. Do not be fooled when people say to use Cheat engine to speeds up DeSmuMe, this is only true for some 64 bit Desktop PC that has multiple cores, Im not saying that people who say cheat engine can speed up your game are wrong but rather it’s not applicable in most cases. Remember cheat engine has or adds another process to your computer in which in effect will also use additional RAM and will most probably lessen the speed of DeSmuMe most especially if you are using a laptop/notebooks.

Tip3: be an Admin and free your ram
It always advisable to run DeSmuMe as an administrator though it does not have a direct relation to game speed but for some svns, this could be very handy, another things is to free your RAM by disabling graphical effects and desktop gadgets of your computer, this will ensure maximal Physical RAM availability, you can do it on windows manually via control panel or you may opt to use 3rd party software Like Tune UP Utilities(most reliable).

Tip 4: Render on Soft Rasterizer and enable textures but if your graphics chip has Open GL support use it .
3d settings- select Soft Rasterizer instead of OpenGl and tick enable textures – the rest under this tab group are optional but just in case you are using a particular svns that programmers to run on OpenGl make sure to follow them and not rant on the world wide web of your slow experience. it does pay of to read documentations as it is very much available to the public to read except some entries on the desmume wiki page(cause some of their entries a way over the top misleading)

Tip 5: Make use of the Hot Key configurations and think about frame skip settings
hot key designated functions of DeSmuMe is most often not used by many people but just so you know this keys works best most especially in tight closed environments and on battles of Pokémon black and white. Like the Fast forward Toggle, which is an on demand on and off faster fps , is very useful in battles as it can speed up transitions. Frame skip setting does not ensure faster game, it only applies to 2d events or graphics that is rendered frame by frame like battles. The higher the Frameskip value is set the less smooth graphics will be rendered. remember pokemon black and white is not 2d
Tip 6: sounds and filters- is actually your preference
The idea is the more bad the sounds the faster the game will be, Need I say more about that? if you want to view the game in a much larger screen I highly suggest to not use filters cause they may look good graphically at a static view but once you move you will see that most of the desmume filters dont actually work or look good in pokemon games.

And lastly
Tip 7: Emulation and wifi settings
A lot of people love to use the wifi simulation in DeSmuMe, but if you want speed, turn off everything under the Bios, firmware and General tab group. Activate the wifi settings only when needed or on demand. External firmware actually adds and additional process for DeSmuMe and that is decrypting the firmware and synching your game data to it constantly while not shutting down DeSmuMe’s own firmware.

Tip 8: Tips 5,6,7 refers to tools
combining the tools from these items is collectively a part of the innate function of desmume which is tool assisted speed running of games or TAS . TASing is a process where in you modify/ manipulate the normal circumstances of a particular game and a desired or accidental effect using a tool or a set of tools. So if you know what is this and how to do it... you will realize my reservations on the faqs in the desmume wiki

in closure these are just my tips for you . at the end of the day there is no actual black and white rule as to what the settings for desmume is. each game has its own and we should be thankful that at least the desmume developers still configures desmume to be compatible for pokemon games

title: thoughts on the possible remake of Pokemon Ruby and Saphire
excerpt: There has been a lot of discussion about the possible remake of the paired versions of Ruby and Sapphire aka the primary games of the third generation of Pokémon. And to be honest I have my mixed feelings about the remak...
content:
There has been a lot of discussion about the possible remake of the paired versions of Ruby and Sapphire aka the primary games of the third generation of Pokémon. And to be honest I have my mixed feelings about the remake, one ,those two games made me stop playing Pokémon and two, is there a need for it? I have strong reservations for the third generation of Pokémon games let alone the Pokémon themselves introduced in generation III had a lot of misses as to in terms of connecting itself to the 1st 2 generations of games.

Now I know there are a lot of fans of the third generation of games, but I think I am one of the few OG(original) players of Pokémon that said , “Ok I need to move- on with my life”. To me playing Pokémon was and still is both combined amusement and fun regardless of what stat my Pokémon has, to me at least at the time when I first started playing my Japanese green version (I did not even know that soon it will be the famous Pokémon game we know) it was simply the act of collection of the 150 Pokémon(mew excluded) and finishing the game , and it follow suite when 2nd gen was introduced. I remember the day when we put so much regard to mew and celebi, how powerful mewtwo was and the hell we care about breeding Pokémon, it was those days that we don’t have wifi battles but we do have our link cables, it was those days that Rare Candies were much even more important than pokeballs, an not to mention MissingNo in Cinnabar islands was a taboo topic as well as even mentioning Visual Boy advance.

Looking Back, designs of the first 2 generations of Pokémon was not about detail but more of individuality of the family line or specie. In my opinion the first 2 generations of Pokémon were very much simple in terms of design and yet it has uniqueness in each and every single one of them.
When the 3rd generation of Pokémon games went out this is what I had in mind
kyogre reminded me so much of whamon while Groudon reminded me so much of Guilmon.

The third gen game felt so distant and disconnected, Ironically set in a distant land of called Hoenn.
The new Game mechanics of pokemon games were all fine to me like the introduction of characteristics, the rise of PID EV and IVs(not exactly sure). it was alright for me but my greatest contention to it is that the new generation of pokemon did not feel like it was pokemon. It felt like digimon of some sort and do not get me wrong, I am both a fan of digimon and pokemon. But with a lot of new things introduced in the new gen that i just started looking for the old 200+ pokemon. while indeed i played ruby then, you cant imagine how much I miss the older gen to the point that my bellsprout was even more valuable than my torchic. it was that bad. there were a lot of instances in the game that i was just breezing through it. at some extent I desperately needed a guide cause I was Just Lost in Hoenn. Mind you the only town that I remember in Hoenn was Littlerot or probably it was not even littlerot. it was just an arghhh point for me about pokemon.
The link cable was replaced by infrared in gameboy advance which i though was good, and then the beauty contest was introduced , graphics had improved way much and other stuff. but my point is simply that the fact that Nintendo Gamfreak sat the bar it too high that there was so much that, it felt that generation 3 was the end of pokemon for me... well at least at that point in time. in addition sales was not as high as the previous two generations.

this down fall of sales lead to the over compensation that Nintendo did with Pokemon Emerald, if you thought Ruby and Sapphire was awesome then Emerald would be epicness. and to top it off so then, gen I fans, made their mouths shut-up when Gamefreak/Nintendo made firered and leafgreen.

Now will I be happy if ruby and sapphire will have a remake version? the answer is not really, but i do hope the enhancements would wow me just like they did in Gen IV and GenV.
Is there a big chance that the remake is possible? I say yes But the odds are not the same as HeartGold and Soul Silver and FireRed and LeafGreen, why? LeafGreen and FireRed were released because it had a very strong purpose for the gaming franchise and that is to connect Gen I pokemon and Gen II Pokemon to Gen III while the HGSS pair were to serve and extent the capabilities of the Nintendo DS and Following up the success of LGFR (money generation/profit for nintendo and gamefreak). the first two gen had such a strong following that its fans crosses people born at least upto early 80's. you know Nintendo gamefreak takes into account its audience quite well .

Now with those two points lets try to add another factor. normally the remakes are game releases based on the response of the fans of every current pokemon generation the idea is, profit expansion amidst success but more recently its seems that the remake pattern might be not a pattern at all, all because of generation V, pokemon Black and White. if you haven't noticed it yet, all of the things nintedo does lately are unexpected stuff, examples are the number of pokemon in gen V, agreeing that Isshu be changed to unova, gen V pokemon has no relation to previous pokemon generations and them developing pokemon black in white and have it featured in DS instead of 3ds and lastly the sudden dropping the price of Nintendo 3ds. so in my opinion if Nintendo does its regular pattern for pokemon games it will be more losses to them, but if they keep the unexpected things then it can catapult them to have more income in the long run.

I cant figure out the purpose of the remake of pokemon ruby and sapphire. It would be much better of they try to make a remake of the third related game to the paired versions like the remake of Yellow, Crystal or Emerald, If Nintendo does try to make a remake of the three games it would be much better in terms of sales .

collectively since the green light for the most gray area of pokemon games, the 3rd game of GenV, is almost at hand. i do wish nintendo would do great in Pokemon Gray, but for the remake of ruby and sapphire ? I say to nintendo to keep your time in the development of the third game of pokemon black and white cause i think there is No urgency for such a remake of Ruby and Sapphire let alone Ninetendo 3ds is not even considered a new generation hand held device

Tell me what you think guys? Do we really need a remake of ruby and sapphire? comment down bellow and share your thoughts

content:
for the updated version of this guide go to desmume-R4Data.htm
This method will allow you to still use cheats you have entered in the game prior to integrating with the r4cheat database. Think of the r4cheat database as storage or library where you can get the codes at anytime.
Things you need
  • Latest SVN of DeSmuMe download it here: http://goo.gl/RSd5M
  • Latest r4cheat database: download it here: http://goo.gl/QCZUE
  • A game (eg: Pokémon black)
Now simply extract the latest SVN of DeSmuMe in to your usual folder of emulator. If this is the first time you are going to use DeSmuMe you have to begin by opening a ROM. In that wat the default folders will be automatically set-upped for you.

The default folders of DeSmuMe are as follows :
AviFiles, Cheats,Roms Firmware,Language, State, Screenshots, Battery and Lua,
Cheats: is where your AR codes and DeSmuMe cheats are stored, this is the folder where we are going to store USRCHEAT.DAT file (the database)
So therefore
  1. Extract the database to the cheats’ folder; make sure to keep its original name.
  2. Now open DeSmuMe and tap the Config Tab and look and click for the submenu “Path Settings” and a dialogue box will open
  3. Look for the R4 cheats database file name and select usrcheat.dat
  4. Then run your game, under the emulation tab select Cheats then list
  5. Cheat list dialogue box will open, on the lower right of the dialogue box click the cheats base menu and the a dialogue box containing Pokémon black codes stored in the r4cheat data base will pop-out
  6. Now from here: select the codes you want to be included on the current DeSmuMe cheat database you are using ; select a code then click add it will prompt you back to the Cheat List dialogue box
  7. Finally the Cheat List dialogue box look for the name of the code you have recently added and that’s it (its ur choice if you want to turn it on or not heheh)
The good thing about the r4 cheat database is that it automatically detects the game you loaded on DeSmuMe using its game ID just like what it does on No$Zoomer an independent addon developed to enhance NO$GBA (because it lacks updates)

Now let me take this opportunity to discuss certain codes that has no value or worth for DeSmuMe
They are the following:
  • Disable 3D Edge Marking
  • Backlight Codes
  • Load ROM and fix saving in No$GBA
The Disable 3D Edge Marking code was specifically developed for no$Gba players. why you ask? The shear 3d software engine that runs no$gba was last updated way back 2008 and from that point on… game developers have developed certain ways on how to make things look or appear on your Nintendo DS screen. A thing that DeSmuMe have successfully responded with, now, what does the code exactly does? Since Pokémon black and white now runs on a 3d environment (sort of) the edges of the sprites of the characters, trees and buildings has a certain degree of light or transparency effect in its colors and edges if the emulator cannot run it then what it would appear to your screen would vary from what you can see in an actual DS as seen in the illustration below.

to put more light into it. your emulator would interpret it wrongfully and hence the effect on the left side of the illustration. programming wise if we disable it will remove the cause of the error graphically. by disabling this would leave us with the bare sprite. its like peter pan not having a shadow or tinker bell not glowing and in effect would give a closer simulation of the screen of a real nintendo ds. the code does not have value for desmume because it is part of the settings of the emulator you can check the 3d settings yourself. regardless of the code desmume can run pokemon ds games with no graphical glitches.

The ds Back light codes is very much self explanatory I guess in terms why it won’t work on DeSmuMe and No$.

Load ROM and fix saving in No$GBA code is specifically made for no$ because it lacks certain load binaries on it if you are gonna ask why? Ill say it again… IT LACKS UPDATES.

On closing, I must say that the move of the programmers of DeSmuMe to include the r4cheat database feature for the emulators is a very smart move and will offer its users more options and capabilities in using DeSmuMe

content:
Upon my quest to study more on HTML and Java script, i accidentally Opened an .exe file that was suspicious enough to begin with, well anyways, it made my computer go onto a blue screen and poof all goes my recent files that I was working on, good thing about it is the I double clicked the file because the malware it self at a certain string was not fully compatible with one another making it me possible to access my safe mode. a few scan with my anti-virus that I tunred off that day and a very long chkdsk function with tune-up utilities and a new user account salvage the remaining of my files and walahh I'm Online again...

*always double check path settings guys

Essentially DS emulation almost is as close to full completion, probably it’s only the Wi-Fi technology that is needed to wrap it up. With this feature absent there are certain things that you cannot actually do on Playing Pokemon trades, evolution of some Pokemon, Entering Wi-Fi Tournaments, accepting Mystery Gifts. On the contrary of it there are actually a lot of ways you can do to enhance your gaming experience and make the work like as if it is was the real deal for you.
Emulators
Probably you have asked yourself what is the Best emulator for Pokemon Ds games? Well about two years ago I began playing Pokemon Ds games through an emulator using NO$GBA. That time NO cash was its peak, point one is the fact that is compatible to GBA game and two it was the fastest in terms of speed while playing the game and three it is easy to use almost the same using VBA.
NO$GBA v 2.6a
NO$GBA was able to transition smoothly from GBA support to NDS support. For the longest time I was using this emulator but the down side of it is since January 2008 it was never updated. A few months later I discovered an add-on that enabled me to use the emulator like VBA, NO$zoomer enables you to play a game at a much larger screen and lets you use graphic filters to further enhance game graphics. It was almost a perfect emulator and actually a force to reckon with in the programming industry.

A good thing to note on this emulator is you can actually run Pokemon Diamond, Pearl and Platinum at full speed with very little graphical distortion. With it many players were able to finish Pokemon DS games using No$. Aside from the Wi-Fi issue , emulation on No$ also was not able to support a key a feature in the game which is the Pal Park, a place in the game that lets you migrate Pokemon form games of the third Generation to Diamond, Pearl and Platinum. However Ideas (another emulator) was able to activate this feature using a special method. I don’t have much info about it for the moment but it was only compatible to Pearl and Diamon only and not to platinum.

This code provided a temporal solution to the problem but come to think of it the realization of things is: this is as far as No$ supporters can go.
On the programming side of things No$GBA 2.6a still supported a generic Battery save file type which is essential for hacking the game and at the same time provided a port / import of battery file for other emulators to use and special programs like PokeSav thus hence came up the rise of No$GBA’s contemporaries ie: IdeaS and DeSmuMe.

The site dictates what will be the stable release in terms of DeSmuMe. Next Point, in the latest release of DeSmuMe, the black screen issue is almost resolved. title: Emulation On my Perspective
excerpt: Emulation of Pokemon games have been around for some time now. In the past, game emulation is always criticized for certain things like copy right infringement, promotion of piracy, stealing of intellectual property and...
content:
Emulation of Pokemon games have been around for some time now. In the past, game emulation is always criticized for certain things like copy right infringement, promotion of piracy, stealing of intellectual property and many more. But throughout the years game emulation has proved to be a type of technology of its own, it went from an ugly disposition into a status symbol for emulator developers to reverse engineer a game and make it compatible to other games itself.
Emulation plays a vital role for games to be successful, some may argue on this, but the good thing about emulators is that it directly/indirectly promotes games and elevates the game’s popularity to a level that it is inarguably a real “Must Have”. Think of this way, it was through young that adults in the 90’s were able to recognize and merit the idea of games and translate them into your Personal computers and vice versa in terms of the advancement of the emulators.
As for the here and now kids who use to own Nintendo Gameboy plus GB Pocket as well as GB color and GBA, play those games from way back when through emulators. Emulator’s is actually an avenue for gamers to play classic game like Super Mario Bro’s Pacman, Bee wWings, Space Invaders, Galaga and many more
As an additional, emulation has very little effects on the market of Nintendo in terms of their income, Why? Well certainly one thing: kids will always be kids even when they are adults they will keep seeking things from their childhood and therefore whatever the advancement of the console they will follow or to the very least influence their own kids to play. As time goes by… every kids from every generation will always would want to have a handheld device, and to top it off the main market of Nintendo Handheld games are kids who have parents who can afford and of course those adults that will always have a piece of youth on their hearts. So therefore Nintendo’s market is as solid as a Diamond.
Needless to say there is a symbiotic relationship between Nintendo Technology and Emulation Technology. Often times most of game reviewers and guide makers use emulation as a substitute for console and handheld gaming. This is due to the fact that you cannot actually own all consoles at the same time.
As a final note, emulation is here to stay forever and I respect this enthusiast to further on and progress this technology. Thank you guys

Migrating Pokemon on Pal Park Via Emulator
For the Past two years the emulation for DS has been slow and yet has a steady progression. There are actually two particular emulators that has moved and re-defined the emulation of DS games that is IdeaS and DeSmuMe. On a perspective Pokemon games almost became the gold standard of measurement of capability of emulators through out the years.

Since the DS emulation technology came out, there are two main key issues that went with it; Wi-Fi access and GBA slot capability. Wi-Fi access gives the capability for a regular hand held game user to access Global trade station enabling users to trade with other gamers all over the world and enable to make some Pokemon evolve into its advance forms, GBA slot on the other hand enable some Pokemon appear in the wild depending to which Pokemon Cartridge is on the GBA slot of DS and of course Pal Park which gives you capability to migrate Pokemon from 3rd Generation of games.

Since emulation is essentially grounded on script language, translating wireless fidelity technology has been difficult, the later, GBA slot capability has a stronger shot in terms in putting into emulation

Pal Park on Emulator
A few months ago I stumble in one of those forums that the emulator IdeaS(or some other emulator) has attained the capability of accessing Pal Park by tweaking certain settings of the emulation and usage of a hex code. The Idea did not stop when I saw a video a few days ago that DeSmuMe has the same feature. So I tried it myself and after a few mishaps it was a success with a 3/6 tries. And as a foot note of it, DeSmuMe released its new version just recently; So I Suggest for people who use emulators to try this one but I must warn you It may or may not work for you:

Requirements:
- Your Computer (Duh!!!), PS I don’t know if this will Work on MAC
-DeSmuMe 0.9.6 x86
- non Patched ROM of 4th generation Game of Pokemon (Diamond, Pearl, Platinum, Heart Gold, Soul Silver)
- a save file of that game preferably the game is on a stage where you have access on Pal Park
- Visual Boy Advance
- non Patched Rom of 3rd generation of games for Sapphire, Ruby, Emerald, Fire Red and Leaf Green
- a save file of that game that is in 128kb format

Settings of the emulators
DeSmuMe 0.9.6 x86
- on the Config Tab you have to adjust certain things to adjust :
- Config>3d setting: Renderer change it to SoftRasterizer, and tick the enable edge marking and last everything else is unticked
- Config>Emulation Setting: just tick enable bus level timing everything else is unticked
- Config> Frame Skip= 3
-Config> DirectDraw SW
-Config> Hot Key Config: change it to your needs

Visual Boy Advance (preferably the non link one)

Activating Pal Park and Migrating Pokemon on Diamond, Platinum, Heart Gold and Soul Silver
*I’ll be using Fire Red and Platinum as an example for Migrating Pokemon*
  1. Place the ROM and save files of the games on the folder/ Location of DeSmuMe
  2. Open the ROM of Fire Red using VBA (make sure to have 6 active Pokemon on PC Box) then save preferably inside a Pokemon Center
  3. Open the ROM of Platinum, make sure to disable cheats while booting the game, then save inside the Pal Park entrance
  4. Now this is the actual attempt, Open your DeSmuMe, Open Pokemon Platinum
  5. On the Emulation Tab click GBA slot, then select Guitar Grip, thick click yes when ask to reset rom
  6. After the reset, on the Emulation Tab again click GBA Slot, then select GBA game then locate Pokemon Fire Red, click yes when asked to reset the game
  7. Lastly let game boot on the title screen on the load section, there should be a menu that will appear Migrate Pokemon Fire Red or something that. And whoolah you can now migrate Pokemon from this game
*With this feature of DeSmuMe it also follows the GBA Slot Pokemon on Pokemon Platinum can be activated (you know those Pokemon that will only appear if a certain cartridge is inserted on DS)
Some notes to follow on Pal Park
  • “- The Pokemon cannot know a HM move. If it does, you will need to delete the move via a Move Deleter in the GBA game.
  • - HG/SS has eliminated the 1 transfer a day rule, meaning you can now transfer your Pokemon over multiple times, but you must go in a catching game and get them before you transfer more.
  • - Although 100% not confirmed, you cannot transfer irregular Pokemon (Such as Glitch Pokemon such as Bag EGG), and you cannot transfer unhatched Egg Pokemon.”(Howell 2010)
  • - Although this should be pretty obvious, you can only transfer Pokemon from the 3rd generation games (Ruby, Sapphire, FireRed, LeafGreen, and Emerald). R/B/Y/G/S/C transfer are NOT compatible
